summary: The three sub-rows are well-argued and every fact I could check is true: CommitDelta really is (long sequence, List<SegmentCommit> segments) with no per-pod flushSeq anywhere in the chain; DefaultIngest.flushSeq is an instance field that restarts at 0 while podShortId is constructor-injected; CheckpointWriter's class javadoc records the process-local window as a known hole in almost these words and CheckpointWriterContentTest.theFirstCheckpointAfterATakeoverCarriesNoPodsAtAll asserts it; ADR-0031 is about two live processes racing an epoch at the lease level and does not answer this; ADR-0033 records the adjacent-uvarint swap hazard; chain-delta-v0.bin and chain-delta-batched-v1.bin both exist; M4.10a is in backlog-done.md; LocalSequencer.epoch() exists. No cost finding: nothing in the three rows adds an object-store request, and the per-pod field M4.10c proposes lands inside a delta that already carries one SegmentCommit per pod, so the object grows with the fleet and the request rate is unchanged (segments and nodes, not records or partitions). What is wrong is the seams. M4.10c's existence is decided before M4.10b's ADR is written; the split names one wire format where the key it is deciding lives in two; and the preserved source row landed under the wrong heading with a stale status.

findings.title: M4.10c presupposes the outcome of the ADR M4.10b exists to write, and the no-format-change alternative is nowhere recorded
findings.detail: M4.10b is written as an open decision ('DECIDE WHAT MAKES THE IDEMPOTENCY KEY DURABLE', 'Decision only, no mechanism'), yet M4.10c is already a committed todo row that hard-codes one answer: the delta must carry flushSeq, as a wire-format change, with a golden and an ADR. The notes make the same assumption ('the key's shape (M4.10b) decides what the delta must carry (M4.10c)') -- what, never whether. There is a concrete alternative the rows never mention: the chain ALREADY carries a per-pod token that survives a restart. Every SegmentCommit holds a segment key rendered by SegmentKey.render as '%s/data/%s/%019d-%s-%016x-h%d-%s.bseg' -- timestampMillis, then podShortId, then a per-pod sequence (SegmentPublisher.java:137 calls it 'per-pod sequence, so it is unique WITHOUT coordination'). The timestamp prefix is exactly the thing flushSeq lacks: it does not restart at 0. CommitLog.commitAll already refuses a batch whose segment keys collide, so the codebase already treats that key as a per-flush identity. Whether it wins is M4.10b's call -- a wall-clock-ordered token has its own objection, and that objection belongs in the ADR's 'Alternatives considered' rather than being skipped.
findings.failure_scenario: Either M4.10b's ADR ratifies the answer already written into M4.10c, in which case the ADR is a formality and sdd.md rule 7 ('a spec is reviewed before code is written') buys nothing; or M4.10b decides the key can be made durable without a new field, and M4.10c -- a chain wire-format change touching every reader, every writer, the fakes, a new golden and a bucket of v0/v1 deltas that outlive the change by the whole retention window, i.e. the single most expensive item in this decomposition -- has already been written as a blocked-only-on-b todo and will be picked up and built. The split exists to stop exactly that.
findings.recommendation: Make M4.10c conditional on M4.10b's decision in both the row and the note ('IF M4.10b's decision requires the delta to carry it'), and name the segment-key alternative in M4.10b's note as something the ADR must consider and record, alongside the lease epoch.

findings.title: The split names ONE wire format, but the key M4.10b decides is carried by Checkpoint too
findings.detail: M4.10c's scope is stated as CommitDelta alone. But the idempotency window is already a persisted format: ADR-0033's Decision is that a checkpoint carries 'per-pod lastAppliedFlushSeq', and Checkpoint (format/src/main/java/binjava/format/Checkpoint.java:41) is 'public record Checkpoint(long sequence, Map<RunKey, StreamOffsets> streams, Map<String, Long> pods)' -- podId String to a bare long, with its own MAGIC 0x42434B50, its own VERSION 0, its own golden checkpoint-v0.bin and its own total-order encoding rule. M4.10b's named candidate is the lease epoch. A Map<String, Long> cannot express (epoch, podId) -> flushSeq without mangling the key string, and neither M4.10b's, M4.10c's nor M4.10d's row or note mentions Checkpoint moving.
findings.failure_scenario: M4.10b's ADR concludes the durable key is (epoch, podId, flushSeq). M4.10c is built to its row and changes CommitDelta only. M4.10d then dedups on a three-part key whose checkpoint-side representation is a two-part map, so a window recovered from a checkpoint compares a bare pair against a qualified key: either the epoch is dropped and a post-restart flushSeq 0 matches a pre-restart flushSeq 0 -- SUPPRESSING A REAL COMMIT, the precise failure the whole task exists to prevent -- or M4.10c grows a second wire format mid-commit, which is the 'is this one commit's worth' question the split was supposed to have settled. Non-negotiable 8 requires the format, every reader, every writer, the fakes, the goldens and the ADR to move in ONE commit; a split that names only one of the two formats carrying the key cannot satisfy it.
findings.recommendation: State in M4.10b's note that its decision determines how many formats move, and in M4.10c's that if the key is widened, Checkpoint (pods: Map<String, Long>, ADR-0033, golden checkpoint-v0.bin) moves in the same commit -- or say explicitly why it does not.

findings.title: The preserved M4.10 source row landed inside the M4.10d section, still marked todo
findings.detail: backlog-notes.md is organised as '### <ID>' immediately followed by that ID's content -- every one of the 60-odd sections in the file, including the M4.6 and M4.8 split precedents. Here the four new prose blocks were inserted under '### M4.10' and pushed the original row down, so it now sits after '### M4.10d' (line 220) and before '### M4.22' (line 233): the full M4.10 source text is, by heading, part of M4.10d's note. It also still reads '| FR-3 | todo |' while backlog.md now says 'split'. M4.6's preserved source row -- the convention this commit followed by keeping banner AND source text -- carries '| FR-11 | split |'. M4.8's own note names this exact failure by name: 'BOTH COPIES OF A SPLIT MUST SAY SO ... which is the one-copy-fixed failure M4.0's archive row names in its own words: fixing ONE copy of a fact and missing its duplicates in the tables that decide what gets built.'
findings.failure_scenario: A session picks M4.10d, follows [notes](backlog-notes.md#m410d) per next-task/SKILL.md ('Read backlog-notes.md only for the task you pick'), and reads to the next heading. It gets M4.10d's two paragraphs PLUS the entire original M4.10 row -- including 'the fix belongs here, with whatever makes the pair durable (the lease's own epoch is the obvious candidate)', which is M4.10b's job. So the reader of the LAST sub-row is told to make the key decision itself, which is the split collapsing back into one task. Symmetrically, a reader following #m410 from the split banner gets the banner and none of the source text, so the clause-by-clause 'nothing was lost' check M4.8's note says M4.6's convention preserves is not actually available under that heading. And next-task's 'Has it already been done? Check the backlog state' hits a row saying M4.10 is todo at full scope while backlog.md says split.
findings.recommendation: Move the '| M4.10 | ... |' row up to directly under '### M4.10', above the split banner or merged into it as M4.6 did, and change its status column from todo to split.

findings.title: 'chain-delta-v2.bin' prescribes a header-version bump where the format's own extension mechanism is a new kind under v1
findings.detail: The golden filenames name the header version each file pins, not a fixture generation: chain-delta-v0.bin is ChainEntry.VERSION_DELTA = 0; chain-delta-batched-v1.bin, chain-seal-v1.bin and chain-continue-v1.bin are all VERSION_KINDED = 1, distinguished by their KIND_* byte. ADR-0028's implementation states the mechanism on ChainEntry itself -- 'Version 1 IS a kinded entry' -- and ADR-0032 took KIND_DELTA = 0 on exactly the terms the reserved comment set out for 'a FUTURE delta layout'. A third delta layout is therefore naturally a new kind under version 1, whose golden would follow chain-delta-batched-v1.bin's shape. 'chain-delta-v2.bin, alongside v0 and the batched v1' reads the three names as a version sequence, and the row's 'Wire-format change: version, ...' repeats it.
findings.failure_scenario: An implementer follows the row literally and adds a third case to ChainEntry.decode's version switch -- a top-level VERSION = 2 that the kind byte exists precisely to avoid -- so every reader of the chain gains a branch, and ADR-0028's decision is contradicted without the ADR M4.10c is required to write ever noticing, because the row told it the answer.
findings.recommendation: Drop the concrete filename, or say 'a new golden, named for whichever the ADR chooses -- a new KIND under v1 (ADR-0028/0032's mechanism) or a new version'.

findings.title: M4.10c cites the empty-pods symptom as its justification but its stated scope does not fix it, and no sub-row owns the tripwire test
findings.detail: M4.10c's row justifies itself with '...its first checkpoint carries no pods, emptying that window exactly when duplicates are likeliest (CheckpointWriter's own javadoc)'. Carrying a field in CommitDelta does not by itself make CheckpointWriter's private Map<String, Long> pods non-empty after a takeover: something must fold the recovered chain into it. That is production work in sequencer, not codec work, and neither M4.10c ('the record, the codec, every reader and writer, the fakes, a new golden, and the ADR') nor M4.10d ('THE DEDUP ITSELF') names it. CheckpointWriterContentTest.theFirstCheckpointAfterATakeoverCarriesNoPodsAtAll was planted with 'Asserting what it ACTUALLY carries is what will make M4.10 notice this rather than inherit it silently' -- and its doesNotContainKey("poda") assertion must be inverted by whichever sub-row fixes the hole. No sub-row says which.
findings.failure_scenario: M4.10c lands as a pure format change, its stated justification (a first checkpoint carrying pods) still false, and the planted assertion still green; M4.10d then lands a dedup whose recovered window is still empty after a takeover, and the tripwire test passes throughout because it asserts the broken behaviour and nobody was told to flip it.
findings.recommendation: Name the owner of seeding CheckpointWriter's pods map from the recovered chain, and name CheckpointWriterContentTest.theFirstCheckpointAfterATakeoverCarriesNoPodsAtAll as the assertion that must be inverted in that same commit.
